subject: English
passage: Writer Kwame Mbalia's love of short fiction began when he read a collection of Zora Neale Hurston's stories as a child, and he would develop into a prolific short story writer himself, publishing pieces like "The Garvey Protocol" (2018) and "Origins" (2015). Yet he's best known as a novelist, in part due to his ______ Strong Punches a Hole in the Sky (2019) winning a Coretta Scott King Author Honor.
prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Choice A is the best answer because the convention being tested is punctuation use with restrictive modifiers. The novel's title is essential information that identifies which specific fantasy novel won the Coretta Scott King Author Honor. When a modifier is restrictive—necessary to identify the specific noun being referenced—no punctuation should separate it from the noun it modifies. The phrase 'his fantasy novel Tristan Strong Punches a Hole in the Sky' correctly follows Standard English conventions by placing the title directly after 'fantasy novel' without any intervening punctuation.
